title: perf(desktop): timeline thumbnails read by Range, cached per recording (audit VID-A3)
body:
## What changed and why

Opening the editor read the whole recording into a `Blob` (`fetch(url).blob()`) just to decode 24 timeline thumbnails (audit finding VID-A3). Now only the container index and the keyframe neighbourhoods the decoder asks for are read, via `Range` requests, and re-opening the same recording decodes nothing.

- `renderer/src/lib/open-recording-input.ts` (new): `openRecordingInput(url)` returns a mediabunny `Input` backed by `UrlSource`. `probe-source.ts` now uses it (signature unchanged).
- `main/media-protocol.ts`: responses add `access-control-expose-headers: content-range, content-length, accept-ranges`. `kaipu-media://` is cross-origin from the page, so CORS hides those headers from `UrlSource`; without `Content-Range` it cannot learn the file size, and a moov-at-end MP4 may degrade to sequential reads. I confirmed by reading the handler that the headers were not exposed before; I did not observe the degradation at runtime.
- `use-source-thumbnails.ts`: opens the recording through the helper (no `fetch`), keeps the 24 JPEG Blobs per `url|duration` in a module LRU of 8, creates object URLs at publish time and revokes them on unmount, and disposes the `Input` in `finally` and on cleanup (mediabunny's `Input.dispose()` is idempotent, checked in `node_modules/mediabunny/src/input.ts`). An empty result is not cached, so a transient failure does not stick.
- `SourceThumbnail { sourceTime, url }` is unchanged, so the timeline lanes need no change.

Not in this PR (phase 2, follow-up): the GIF and export workers still take a `Blob`. Gate for it: confirm a Worker can `fetch` `kaipu-media://` with `Range: bytes=0-9` and get a 206.

## Plan file

The plan (`plans/audit-2026-10-15/28-video-thumbnails-range.md`) and its `00-index.md` row live on `docs/code-audit-2026-10-15` (PR #301), not on `main`, so there is nothing to delete here. Whoever merges #301 should drop that plan file and its index row.

## How I verified it

- `bun run verify` from the repo root, twice in a row: exit 0 both times. The second run was fully cached by Turbo, so it did not re-execute the tests; the first run did.
- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/src/features/video-editor` (59 files, 591 tests, run before the last formatting-only change) and the new `use-source-thumbnails.test.ts` (6 tests: no `fetch` and 24 timestamps starting at `0.5/24 × duration`; dispose on success and on no video track; cache hit on second mount; revoke count equals create count; duration is part of the key; eviction past 8).
- Tests mock `mediabunny` and the helper at the boundary, as `generate-thumbnail.test.ts` does, so they cover the orchestration, not real Range traffic.

**Not done:** the DevTools measurement from the plan (Task 3) needs the running Electron app and a long recording. The 15–50 MB figure is the plan's estimate, not a measurement. The Playwright desktop E2E suite was not run locally (CI runs it).

## How to test it yourself

1. Run the desktop app (`bun run dev` in `apps/kaipu-record`) and open a long recording (several hundred MB if you have one) in the editor.
2. Open DevTools → Network, filter on `kaipu-media`. Expect only 206 responses, no single 200 of file size, and `access-control-expose-headers` on the responses.
3. Sum the 206 body sizes and compare with the file size. Please report the numbers on this PR.
4. Close the editor and reopen the same recording: no new thumbnail range requests, and the timeline lanes fill immediately.
5. Optionally check `chrome://blob-internals` for a file-sized blob (there should be none) and time editor mount to filled lanes against `main`.

Refs NIW2-403

Run: Gas City session ni-wisp-yooa8fp, bead ka-9fi, Mac mini
